# Parallelism, GPU, restart/IO and reproducibility {#sec-ch14}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy); kintera@c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77

This chapter describes how snapy runs on several processes and devices, how it writes output and restart files, and
which of its results the tests show to be reproducible. It has three parts. The first covers parallel execution and
the GPU[^rg-035e9ee3c42d]: how processes are launched and meet, which communication backends carry the messages, how the messages
of a ghost exchange are matched, how several blocks share a process and its GPU streams, which decisions are
reduced over all ranks, and what changes on a CUDA[^rg-7d5758f753ba] device. The second covers output and restart: per-block NetCDF
files and their combine, PnetCDF, restart files and resume, output scheduling and statistics, and the
post-processing tools. The third is an inventory of the reproducibility claims and their evidence. What a ghost cell
contains is the subject of @sec-ch03 (in particular @sec-ch03-exchange); here only how it gets there is
described. Code citations resolve at the book's code pin, `chengcli/snapy`
`919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` (`code_pin.yml`). The schemes are listed in @tbl-ch14-schemes.

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| launch and rendezvous (@sec-ch14-launch) | env `MASTER_PORT`, `RANK`, ... | one process | n/a | `test_process_group` |
| communication backends (@sec-ch14-backends) | env `BACKEND` | `ucx` on Linux, `gloo` on macOS | exact copy | `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam_gloo` |
| exchange message matching (@sec-ch14-msgmatch) | `SyncOptions.phyid` | 0 | exact copy | `test_exchange` |
| several blocks per process (@sec-ch14-bpp) | `distribute: blocks_per_process` | 1 | n/a | `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` |
| collectives and global decisions (@sec-ch14-collectives) | none | on with several processes | exact (MIN, MAX) | `test_check_redo_parallel` |
| GPU execution (@sec-ch14-gpu) | CMake `CUDA`, env `DEVICE` | CPU[^rg-0ab3aad6818c] | round-off | `test_vic_moist_device_python` |
| NetCDF output and combine (@sec-ch14-netcdf) | `outputs: type: netcdf` | float, combined | exact, then float | `test_output_barrier` |
| PnetCDF output (@sec-ch14-pnetcdf) | `outputs: type: pnetcdf` | off | float | none |
| restart files (@sec-ch14-restart) | `outputs: type: restart`, `-r` | off | exact | `test_restart_cycle_limit` |
| output scheduling and statistics (@sec-ch14-schedule) | output `dt`[^rg-21fdabf0cfa6] | `dt: 0` | exact for the sampled states | `test_user_output` |
| combine and inspect tools (@sec-ch14-tools) | command line | n/a | n/a | none |
| reproducibility inventory (@sec-ch14-repro) | none | n/a | n/a | see @tbl-ch14-repro-claims |

: The schemes of this chapter. "exact copy" means the bytes arrive unchanged. Test names omit the `.release` suffix
of C++ entries. {#tbl-ch14-schemes}
